A casement window is a frame split into panes, called lights, that are either fixed or hinged at the side or top. You can combine them in almost any layout, so casements suit 1930s semis, new-build extensions and most homes in between. They are usually the most cost-effective way to replace old timber, aluminium or tired uPVC.
